A1. An external researcher must request a study appointment ten working days in advance and provide institution, object identifiers, and purpose.
A2. A staff member must supervise the study visit. Personal bags stay in the locker. Only pencils and approved cameras can enter the study room.
A3. Personal reference photography is allowed when the registrar approves it. Publication photography requires a separate written license. Flash is prohibited.
A4. If a visitor finds damage, isolate the display and notify the duty conservator immediately. The supervisor completes an incident record before shift end.
A5. Security reviews access logs monthly. Staff may request a badge reset from their supervisor; badge issuance times are not specified.

E1. Store paper objects at 45 to 55 percent relative humidity. Store metal objects at 35 to 45 percent. The wood store has a separate 45 to 60 percent band.
E2. A reading out of range for 30 consecutive minutes requires a conservation ticket. Include the space, latest reading, start time, and object materials.
E3. Paper displays have a 50-lux lighting limit. Metal displays have a 150-lux limit. Turn off case lighting when the gallery closes.
E4. Check gallery humidity sensors each Monday. Record test results in the equipment log and tell facilities if a sensor fails.
E5. Water near a collection object requires an immediate call to the duty conservator. When safe, keep visitors out of the affected space while awaiting instructions.

L1. A proposed incoming loan is logged 30 calendar days before its planned arrival. The registrar records the lender, object identifiers, arrival date, insurance limits, and a named contact.
L2. Complete the condition report before unpacking ends. It includes painted surfaces, mount integrity, and dated photographs. Both receiving staff sign it.
L3. Transit damage is photographed and reported to the registrar within two working hours of discovery. Do not treat or clean the object before instructions arrive.
L4. A high-value loan requires registrar and finance approval before transport booking. High value means declared value over 50,000 currency units. A standard loan needs registrar approval only.
L5. On final return, send the lender a signed receipt and archive the return report with the entry report.

M1. Book internal movements two working days in advance. The booking includes the object identifier, destination, route, time, and names of both handlers.
M2. Each internal move requires two trained handlers. For freestanding objects heavier than 20 kilograms, a padded trolley is also mandatory.
M3. Close the gallery to visitors during a move across a public floor. Reopen it after the lead handler confirms the path is clear.
M4. Outgoing transit uses a rigid crate and an external shock indicator. Record the indicator seal number before dispatch.
M5. The receiving handler verifies the object identifier against the movement log and signs at destination. The registrar updates the location once both signatures are recorded.
